brief: Morgan Stanley decomposes the implied volatility surface into at-the-money level, 25-delta risk reversal for skew, and 25-delta butterfly for curvature, extended across maturities. Those factors are correlated, 57 to 74 percent on three-day changes in SPX, so naively stacking standard option structures duplicates one exposure rather than diversifying. The correlation is also the opportunity: shorting one correlated factor hedges the common volatility component while the other factor's premium is retained. In SPX, structural put demand against covered-call supply steepens skew, leaving implied spot-volatility covariance above the covariance later realized. A gamma-neutral 3-month 25-delta risk reversal, long vanna and long rega, has a 0.72 Sharpe ratio since 2008 but runs 59 percent correlated with selling 1-month ATM straddles. Adding a long 1-month ATM straddle overlay raises Sharpe 19 percent, cuts maximum drawdown 38 percent, and takes that correlation to minus 2 percent. The MS Equity Skew/Vanna indices implement this: tail-hedged MSVCSKSP shows 10.1 percent CAGR, 8.9 percent volatility, 1.13 Sharpe and 9.8 percent maximum drawdown, against 11.1, 11.6, 0.96 and 28.2 for MSVCSKS2. The daily-unwind test is a factor-isolation exercise, not an implementable strategy, and its returns are gross of costs.
